resources.string:
With a non-original cable, the phone and charger sometimes fail their fast-charge handshake. The phone stays stuck showing the charging bolt while almost no power flows, so the battery still drains. A restart fixes it because it resets the charging chip.

Without root, this app uses Shizuku (ADB-level rights) to command the USB-C port: it limits power, resets the port, or swaps the power role, which can force the charger to handshake again. It measures the current after each try and remembers the one that works on your phone. With root it can also switch the charging input off and on directly.

If nothing works: unplug, restart the phone, then plug in. Also worth trying by hand: with the charger plugged in, turn OTG on and off in Settings (search "OTG"). Long term, use a good cable rated for your OnePlus charger (SUPERVOOC/Warp cables have extra contacts). Cheap cables cause exactly this.

How to start Shizuku (no PC needed, about 2 minutes, once after every phone restart):

1. Connect to any Wi-Fi.
2. Settings → About device → Version → tap "Build number" 7 times to unlock Developer options.
3. Settings → System settings → Developer options → turn on "Wireless debugging".
4. Open Shizuku → "Start via Wireless debugging" → "Pairing", then in Wireless debugging tap "Pair device with pairing code" and type the code into Shizuku's notification.
5. In Shizuku tap "Start". Come back here and tap "Grant permission".
